Warm-started GWR-SCAD and GWR-MCP paths

Source: R/nonconvex-path.R
gwr_nonconvex_path.Rd

Fits a decreasing nonconvex regularization path. Local neighborhoods and centered design columns are reused. Warm starts, persistent active sets, sequential candidate screening, and a complete inactive-coordinate objective-improvement scan reduce work while retaining a coordinatewise minimum check at every accepted solution.

Usage

gwr_nonconvex_path(
  x,
  y,
  coords = NULL,
  neighbors = NULL,
  k = NULL,
  kernel = c("bisquare", "gaussian", "exponential", "tricube", "boxcar"),
  bandwidth = NULL,
  lambda = NULL,
  n_lambda = 50L,
  lambda_min_ratio = 0.001,
  penalty = c("scad", "mcp"),
  gamma = NULL,
  standardize = TRUE,
  screening = TRUE,
  keep_coefficients = FALSE,
  return_diagnostics = FALSE,
  ebic_gamma = 0.5,
  control = gwrs_control()
)

gwr_scad_path(x, y, ..., gamma = 3.7)

gwr_mcp_path(x, y, ..., gamma = 3)

Arguments

x

Numeric design matrix without an intercept.

y

Numeric response vector.

coords

Optional coordinate matrix used to construct neighbors.

neighbors

Optional reusable object from [gwr_neighbors()].

k

Number of neighbors when `neighbors` is not supplied.

kernel

Spatial kernel.

bandwidth

Fixed distance bandwidth. The default `NULL` uses the farthest retained neighbor as an adaptive bandwidth at each target.

lambda

Nonnegative regularization strength.

n_lambda

Number of automatically generated values.

lambda_min_ratio

Ratio of the smallest to largest generated value.

penalty

Nonconvex penalty, either `"scad"` or `"mcp"`.

gamma

Concavity parameter. The default is `3.7` for SCAD and `3` for MCP. SCAD requires `gamma > 2`; MCP requires `gamma > 1`.

standardize

Whether predictors are standardized globally before the local fits. Coefficients are returned on the original scale.

screening

Whether to use sequential screening. A full KKT scan is always performed, so screened variables that violate optimality are restored before a solution is accepted.

keep_coefficients

Whether to retain the full locations-by-coefficients-by-lambda array. The default avoids a potentially large allocation.

return_diagnostics

Whether to compute conditional smoother traces, information criteria, and post-selection refit diagnostics along the path. These use `O(n * length(lambda))` memory and do not require retaining the coefficient cube.

ebic_gamma

EBIC model-space multiplier in `[0, 1]`.

control

Numerical controls from [gwrs_control()].

...

Additional arguments passed by [gwr_scad_path()] or [gwr_mcp_path()] to `gwr_nonconvex_path()`.

Value

An object inheriting from `gwrs_nonconvex_path` and `gwrs_path`.

Details

In guarded-block mode, a failed target stops its remaining lambda path. `path_state` labels converged, failed and unattempted target/lambda entries; `solver_diagnostics` retains objectives, stopping diagnostics and compact pair/block counters. Failed coefficients, if requested, are diagnostic iterates only; invalid fitted values and incomplete-path statistical summaries are unavailable. A warning identifies partial paths. The coordinate mode retains the original behavior.

Examples

quake <- datasets::quakes[1:30, ]
coords <- as.matrix(quake[, c("long", "lat")])
x <- as.matrix(quake[, c("depth", "stations")])
path <- gwr_mcp_path(
  x, quake$mag, coords = coords, k = 18,
  lambda = c(0.2, 0.08, 0.02),
  control = gwrs_control(n_threads = 1, diagnostics = "none")
)
path
path$path_summary
